ep_bva: One possible example is package-version filtering (packaging SpecifierSet.filter). With a final-only specifier such as >=2.0, prereleases=None keeps matching prereleases only when no matching final survives; prereleases=True or False changes that policy. A final outside the specifier must not suppress an otherwise matching prerelease. Useful ideas might compare candidate lists [2.1a1], [1.9,2.1a1] and [2.1a1,2.1], in either order, then consider explicit policy overrides. These classes depend on policy and the filtered candidate set, not separate numeric intervals alone. A plausible fault is checking for any final before applying the specifier. A prerelease/final transition can suggest extra boundary tests. This illustrates possible reasoning, not required class names or a complete suite; use other ideas when better.
decision_table: For example, HTTP response preconditions (Werkzeug Response.apply_conditions) combine method, validators and time. If-Match uses strong ETag comparison and, when present, takes precedence over If-Unmodified-Since. If-None-Match uses weak comparison; a match gives 304 for GET/HEAD but 412 for other methods. Its presence suppresses If-Modified-Since even when it does not match. Possible discriminating pairs use a matching strong If-Match with an otherwise failing date, a weakly matching If-None-Match under GET versus PUT, or a nonmatching If-None-Match with a date that alone would give 304. These can expose wrong precedence or merging rules across method-dependent actions. This is one source of test ideas, not a required table shape; only group conditions supported by the actual specification.
